issues.reason: The reviewer's own q2 names the driver — no rule attaches a PP complement to a copular nominal predicate — and the calibration line accepts improvisation in that gap: the fused opaque property and its decomposition atoms are all true of the sentence and well-typed.

The singular predicate nominal 'a popular subject' over the plural kind predicates of the kind as a whole — KindProperty's stated purpose ('a property of the KIND / population as a whole') — whereas Inheritance would distribute to every hit man the false claim of individually being a popular TV-movie subject.

The unreachability of tv_movie flows from the same uncovered PP-complement construction (no decomposition rule exposes an object buried in a PP), so this mistakes a coverage gap for a parse defect; no emitted atom is false or ill-typed.

Given the gap-forced fusion, the compound-kind rule mandates exposing a gradable adjectival modifier ('expose it iff it is an adjectival property of the referent'), and the never-fuse-incidental-description rule governs typing a referent's kind symbol, not an uncovered predicate-nominal property.

gaps_confirmed: predicate nominal carrying a PP complement ('X is a subject for Y') — no rule attaches the PP to a copular nominal predicate
new_gaps: no decomposition route exposes the object of a PP buried in a fused compound, so tv_movie stays unreferable
notes: The KindProperty-vs-Inheritance call is borderline under the literal could-one-individual-hold-it test, but the number mismatch (plural kind, singular 'a subject') marks a collective kind-level predication, and avoiding false distribution is what KindProperty exists for.
